frontier.hypothesis: A byte-free 4th reference to out2 in the BETWEEN-LOOPS block closes the function outright: all five contested seats, all 132 instructions and the frame size are already target, and the single residual (slot 72, `move $s3,$s6` vs `addiu $s3,$s7,0x20`) exists only because that 4th reference is currently spent as the copy `out3 = out2;`.
frontier.mechanism: flow.c fixes reg_n_refs and reg_live_length BEFORE combine runs, so any out2 mention in that block which combine subsequently deletes is a free +1 reference and a free +5 live length. combine deletes only an insn whose destination is used exactly once and dies in the combining insn, and only within one basic block - so the consumer must be one of the six insns target emits between the loops (`addiu $s1,$s1,0x6C`, `addiu $s2,$s2,0x6C`, `addiu $s4,$zero,0x12`, `lw $t0,0x18($sp)`, `addiu $s3,$s7,0x20`, `addiu $s0,$t0,0x750`).
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate C spellings in which one of those six values is written as a single-use function of out2 that combine folds back to its target form - the most promising is out3 itself, spelled so the copy from out2 has exactly one consumer at combine time. For each, dump .combine and grep for the deleted-insn record BEFORE trusting the sandbox score, then confirm out2 still reads `4 times across 47 insns` in .lreg.

frontier.hypothesis: Attack the tie from tbl's side instead: shrink tbl's reg_live_length from 47 to <= 42 so that an out2 carrying its 4th reference INSIDE loop1 (live 42, pri 1904.8) still loses the tie to tbl, which would let out3 be defined from a4 and emit `addiu $s3,$s7,0x20` directly.
frontier.mechanism: tbl measures 4 refs / live 47, of which 41 is loop1's block and 6 is a block-0 lead-in from its `lui/addiu %hi/%lo` symbol definition. At 4/42 tbl reaches 1904.8 and ties-or-beats an in-loop1 out2 at the same value, with allocno 79 < 86 winning the tie. s7 measured that moving the tbl source statement does NOT move that lead-in, so some pass places it - identify the pass rather than guessing.
frontier.next_probe: Dump .rtl, .cse2 and .loop for func_80041188, locate tbl's definition insn and count insns from it to loop1's code_label to confirm the 6-insn lead-in, then look for a source form whose tbl definition is emitted later in that stream. Verify with `Register NN used 4 times across NN insns` in .lreg before scoring. Note the `tbl sym-K` chain from s4 is an invention and is NOT the route here - this is about placement, not extra references.

frontier.hypothesis: The `pa4 = a4` param-local alias is load-bearing (dropping it costs 1 -> 13) and should be replaced by a spelling whose semantics a reviewer can read, rather than merely kept.
frontier.mechanism: The alias changes which pseudo carries a4 and hence a4's reg_n_refs (6 with the alias), which is one of the four numbers in the priority table that decides the contested seats.
frontier.next_probe: Diff .lreg for candidate.c against rejected/no-pa4-param-alias.c and record exactly which pseudo's refs/live changed. Then test whether a natural typed spelling of the same thing - e.g. taking the pointer through a typed local such as a matrix/vector pointer, consistent with a4 being two 0x20-byte objects - reproduces the same numbers; if it does, prefer it in candidate.c.
